label: Kimi K3.1 Pro
output:
Hi Mikaela, yes we’re doing it. I’ll give you the proper version, warts and all, because it definitely hasn’t been free but it’s made a huge difference here.

We’ve got 290 cows, mostly 3-way crossbreds. We started on 21 September, after mating had started. We skip the Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday arvo milkings, plus Sunday arvo, so those are our four once-a-day milkings each week. Morning milking is 5.15 every day.

On production, our milksolids are down about 6% on the same weeks last year, going off the Fonterra app. Our rep had told us to expect an 8–10% hit, so it’s been better than we were braced for, but 6% is still 6%. Also bear in mind that’s where we are now, not a finished full-season figure. And because we started in September, I wouldn’t take our number as a guarantee of what you’d get starting after Christmas.

The cells did go up. We went from around 110,000 to about 180,000 in the first three weeks. They’re back around 135,000 now, so they’ve settled a lot but they’re not quite back where we started. You have to be really on your game with teat spraying and checking cows on the skip days, or it bites you.

The worst thing that’s happened was a heifer with mastitis going bad on a skipped arvo. We didn’t pick her up until the next morning and she lost a quarter. That was a proper reminder that you can’t just treat the skipped milking as though everything looks after itself until morning.

On the other side, lameness is massively better. We’ve only got four on the lame list now compared with 11 this time last year. Our walk to the back paddocks is 1.8km, so I reckon fewer trips has helped a lot. If Tom’s knees are stuffed, the arvos off will probably help him more than anything else you could change around the place.

It’s helped the staff too. Kieran, our 2IC, said it’s the first spring he hasn’t wanted to quit by October. And on our first skipped Sunday arvo, Dave and me went to Hamilton to see the grandkids. It was my first Sunday off in spring in 20-odd years, which sounds a bit pathetic when you write it down but there you go.

The cows came round quicker than I expected. We had about four days of them bellowing at the gate and thinking we’d lost our minds, then they were fine.

Honestly, I wouldn’t go back. For us, the hours alone are worth the 6%, but that’s us weighing up the production loss against Dave and me, Kieran, and the cows’ feet. I’m not going to tell you it’ll automatically suit your place because the cell count and mastitis side is real, and you can’t be casual about it.

I’ll bring the shed rosters and our numbers to the field day at the Kerrisons’ on the 19th if you want to have a proper look. Or just ring me — much easier than me trying to text all this with my thumbs!
